sentences.en: And welcome back to the psychology of your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s, and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《二十岁的心理学》，在这个播客里，我们探讨二十岁时的一些重大人生变化和过渡，以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, I am so glad that you are here.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你们身处世界何方，我都很高兴你们能在这里。

sentences.en: Thank you for tuning in.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们的收听。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us for another episode of the psychology of your 20s.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们加入我们这一期的《二十岁的心理学》。

sentences.en: This week, we're going to talk about something that is highly personal to me at the moment, and something that I've never spoken about on the show before.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们要谈论一个目前对我个人而言非常私人的话题，也是我以前从未在节目中谈论过的话题。

sentences.en: Despite it being a massive part of my value set, despite it being a massive belief of mine, a massive ethos, and that is why we should take risks in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 尽管它是我的价值观中非常重要的一部分，尽管它是我的一个重大信念、一个重大的准则，那就是为什么我们应该在二十岁时去冒险。

sentences.en: Why it is so important to step out of our comfort zone, to push the boundaries of what we think we are capable of, to just see what happens,
sentences.zh: 为什么走出舒适区、突破我们认为自己能力的极限、去看看会发生什么如此重要，

sentences.en: to explore the possibilities that this life and this earth and this decade really provides us.
sentences.zh: 去探索这个生命、这个地球和这个十年真正为我们提供的可能性。

sentences.en: This has been really on my mind recently.
sentences.zh: 最近我一直在思考这个问题。

sentences.en: For those of you who don't know, I don't do this podcast full-time.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不知道的人，我并不是全职做这个播客的。

sentences.en: I have a job.
sentences.zh: 我有工作。

sentences.en: I have a full-time job.
sentences.zh: 我有一份全职工作。

sentences.en: I work nine to five in an office,
sentences.zh: 我在办公室朝九晚五地工作，

sentences.en: and that was until recently.
sentences.zh: 直到最近。

sentences.en: I have quit my job.
sentences.zh: 我已经辞职了。

sentences.en: I resigned.
sentences.zh: 我辞职了。

sentences.en: And it has really made me rethink my relationship with risk and reinforce how important it is to take advantage of the opportunity that this decade provides.
sentences.zh: 这让我真正重新思考了自己与风险的关系，并强化了利用这十年所提供的机会是多么重要。

sentences.en: And that is to make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 那就是去犯错。

sentences.en: That is to really go out into the world and try as many things as possible.
sentences.zh: 那就是真正走进这个世界，尽可能多地尝试各种事情。

sentences.en: And I think it's important to note that it's not just me saying this from a personal perspective, but so much of the psychology and the science and the unconscious explanations
sentences.zh: 我认为重要的一点是，这不仅仅是我个人的观点，大量的心理学、科学以及科学为我们提供的潜意识解释，

sentences.en: that science provides us really justifies this.
sentences.zh: 都真正证明了这一点。

sentences.en: And it justifies this pattern of behavior to take control of your 20s and use it and use this time and use these opportunities to take risks and see what's out there.
sentences.zh: 它证明了这种掌控二十岁、利用这段时间和这些机会去冒险并看看外面世界的行为模式是合理的。

sentences.en: I think it's such a valuable decade for many reasons, one of them being that our 20s are so unique in that the only person we're normally and I would say
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常有价值的十年，原因有很多，其中之一就是我们的二十岁非常独特，因为我们通常——我想说，

sentences.en: usually only accountable to is ourselves.
sentences.zh: 通常只对自己负责。

sentences.en: We don't have children.
sentences.zh: 我们没有孩子。

sentences.en: Most of us don't have mortgages.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人没有抵押贷款。

sentences.en: There are no looming responsibilities, I would say, for most of us.
sentences.zh: 我想对我们大多数人来说，没有什么迫在眉睫的责任。

sentences.en: Of course, there are instances in which people, you know, get houses young or they have financial debt from taking out student loans or they need to look after a parent who is ill.
sentences.zh: 当然，也有一些情况，比如人们年轻时就买了房，或者因为申请学生贷款而背负经济债务，或者需要照顾生病的父母。

sentences.en: But I would say in general, this decade is defined, it is characterized by freedom.
sentences.zh: 但我认为总的来说，这十年是由自由来定义的，以自由为特征。

sentences.en: So I really want to explore that today and I really want to encourage people through this podcast, through what I'm going to speak on, to take risks, to embrace being uncomfortable
sentences.zh: 所以我今天真的很想探讨这一点，我真的很想通过这个播客，通过我将要讲述的内容，鼓励人们去冒险，去拥抱这十年的不适，

sentences.en: in this decade, to embrace the unknown.
sentences.zh: 去拥抱未知。

sentences.en: I want to talk about why it's absolutely crucial that during this decade, we embrace the opportunity of freedom.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈为什么在这十年里，拥抱自由的机会是绝对至关重要的。

sentences.en: We embrace the opportunity of being, I think, not tied down.
sentences.zh: 我们拥抱那种我认为是不受束缚的机会。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about identity, about unbounded versus bounded risk, existential dread as your friend rather than your enemy, and about regret and how the psychology of regret
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论身份、无界限与有界限的风险、作为朋友而非敌人的存在主义焦虑，以及关于遗憾，以及遗憾的心理学，

sentences.en: actually should compel us to take risks rather than avoid them.
sentences.zh: 实际上应该促使我们去冒险，而不是回避风险。

sentences.en: Like I said, it's just such a pertinent topic for me.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，这对我来说是一个非常切题的话题。

sentences.en: It's just so crazy how life works out.
sentences.zh: 生活的发展方式真是太疯狂了。

sentences.en: You know, the job that I was previously working was my dream job.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我之前做的那份工作曾是我的梦想工作。

sentences.en: It was the thing that I always thought that I wanted and it kind of got to a point where I realized it wasn't my dream anymore, doing this show full time, being able to have
sentences.zh: 那是我一直认为自己想要的东西，但后来我意识到它不再是我的梦想了，全职做这个节目，能够与人们进行精彩的对话，利用这个平台，

sentences.en: amazing conversations with people, using this platform.
sentences.zh: 那才是我的梦想。

sentences.en: That was my dream.
sentences.zh: 生活瞬间就会改变，有时你真的需要勇气去抓住、去把握、去紧紧抓住生活抛给你的机会。

sentences.en: And life changes in an instant and sometimes you need to really have the courage to grasp and grab and cling on to the opportunities that life throws you.
sentences.zh: 我还认为，因为疫情，因为新冠，我们很多二十多岁的人在封锁和这种在全球肆虐的疾病中失去了宝贵的几年，

sentences.en: I also think that because of the pandemic, because of COVID, a lot of us in our 20s lost valuable years to lockdown and to this disease that was running rampant across the globe
sentences.zh: 并且想要保持安全。

sentences.en: and wanting to be safe.
sentences.zh: 我们意识到我们失去了宝贵的几年，失去了二十岁中宝贵的几年，我们想要弥补回来。

sentences.en: And we've had this realization that we've lost valuable years, valuable years of our 20s that we want to make up.
sentences.zh: 而这其中的一部分就是重构我们的叙事和对生活的视角，变得更加勇于冒险。

sentences.en: And part of that is a reframing of our narrative and our perspective towards our lives to be more risk-taking.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很想讨论并剖析所有背后的心理学和科学，为什么我们应该在二十岁时去冒险。

sentences.en: So I really want to discuss and I want to break down all of the psychology, all of the science behind why it is that we should take risks in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 我

sentences.en: I
sentences.zh: 认为我们二十岁的一个重要部分，我们在这十年里必须完成的一项巨大任务，就是弄清楚我们是谁，弄清楚我们想要什么样的生活，弄清楚我们的身份。

sentences.en: think a huge part of our 20s, a huge job that we have to do in this decade is figuring out who we are, figuring out what we want from our lives, figuring out our identity.
sentences.zh: 这并不总是容易的。

sentences.en: And that doesn't always come easy.
sentences.zh: 我认为在过去的几十年、过去的几代人中，以一种非常线性的方式看待生活是很容易的。

sentences.en: I think previously in past decades, in past generations, it was very easy to look at our lives in a very linear sense.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们高中毕业，也许上了大学，遇到了想一起生孩子的人，买了房，和他们生了孩子，工作

sentences.en: You know, we graduated high school, maybe we went to university, we met someone that we wanted to have kids with, we bought a home, we had children with them, we worked
sentences.zh: 到65岁，然后退休，我们就这样完成了人生。

sentences.en: till the age of 65 and then we retired and we were kind of done.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的是，很多人正在反抗那种叙事，反抗那种传统的、常规的生活方式。

sentences.en: And it's really interesting that a lot of people are pushing back against that narrative and pushing back against that conventional, traditional way of going about life.
sentences.zh: 而这种反应以及我们看到的更多的那种行为模式的一部分，就是一种冒险的倾向。

sentences.en: And part of that reaction and part of that pattern of behavior that we're seeing more of is a propensity to take risk.
sentences.zh: 更多的人正在展现自我，做一些我认为在过去可能不仅是不可接受，而且是冒险的事情。

sentences.en: More individuals are putting themselves out there and doing things that I think previously would have been not so much unacceptable, but risky.
sentences.zh: 这会被视为有点危险。

sentences.en: It would have been seen as a bit dangerous.
sentences.zh: 而这些决定变得越来越普遍，也越来越受欢迎。

sentences.en: And those decisions have become a lot more common and a lot more popular.
sentences.zh: 想到我生活中的人，想到我那些已经迈出这一步的朋友，他们决定以非传统的方式做事，

sentences.en: It's so interesting to me to think about the people in my life, to think about the friends that I have who have made the leap, who have made the decision to do things
sentences.zh: 这对我来说非常有趣，他们决定去旅行，决定推迟上大学去做点什么，去做点不同的事情，去探索他们的热情，搬到

sentences.en: in an untraditional way, who have decided to travel, who have decided to put off going to uni and do something, do something different, to explore their passions and to move it
sentences.zh: 不同的城市和不同的国家，只是为了看看那是什么样的。

sentences.en: to different cities and different countries just to see what it's like.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些决定在这十年里非常有价值。

sentences.en: I think that those decisions are so valuable during this decade.
sentences.zh: 我在节目中经常谈论这一点，但我们的二十岁之所以如此具有塑造性且如此重要，是因为这是我们很多身份建立的时候，我们的大脑

sentences.en: I talk about this a lot on the show, but the reason why our 20s are so formative and so important is it's because when a lot of our identity is established, our brain
sentences.zh: 直到25岁才完全发育成熟。

sentences.en: does not fully develop until the age of 25.
sentences.zh: 所以我们二十岁的早期，特别是对于20到25岁之间的人来说，那段时间是你大脑仍在发育、仍在完全形成的时候，

sentences.en: So that early part of our 20s, especially for the people between the ages of 20 and 25, that period is when your brain is still developing and your brain is still fully forming
sentences.zh: 以塑造你将要成为的那个人。

sentences.en: to create the person that you are going to become.
sentences.zh: 这种发展的一部分就是做出你认为最能影响你生活的决定。

sentences.en: Part of that development is making decisions that you think are going to best impact your life.
sentences.zh: 那些决定，就像我说的，并不总是容易的。

sentences.en: those decisions, like I said, are not always going to be easy.
sentences.zh: 这十年，我认为特别是这一代人，被赋予了更多的机会。

sentences.en: This decade, and I think especially this generation, has been afforded with so many more opportunities.
sentences.zh: 我们几周前谈到了选择过载，以及因为我们在这十年里必须做出的决定而感到瘫痪。

sentences.en: We talked about this a couple of weeks ago about choice overload and about kind of being paralysed by the decisions that we have to make in this decade.
sentences.zh: 但通常，其中一些决定会涉及风险，而这种风险有时被计算为能给我们带来最好的回报。

sentences.en: But often, some of those decisions will involve risk and that risk is sometimes calculated to be bringing us the best reward.
sentences.zh: 当谈到权衡风险的收益与成本时，对于我们想要承担的风险，我认为有一种功利主义的观点非常有价值。

sentences.en: When it comes to kind of weighing up the benefits versus the costs of a risk, of a risk that we want to take, there is this idea of utilitarianism that I think is really valuable.
sentences.zh: 它在哲学中被广泛使用和讨论，但我确实认为当我们谈论二十岁的心理学时，它仍然非常重要。

sentences.en: It's used and talked about a lot in philosophy, but I do think it still is really important when we talk about the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 本质上，这个观点是，我们的大脑会基于对风险与回报或成本与收益的评估，为我们做出最合乎逻辑和理性的决定。

sentences.en: Essentially, the idea is that our brain will come to the most logical and rational decision for us based on an assessment of risk versus reward or cost versus benefit.
sentences.zh: 这确实值得考虑，特别是在我们谈论在二十岁做出宏大、令人兴奋且冒险的决定时。

sentences.en: It's something to really consider, especially when we talk about making grand and exciting and risky decisions in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 例如，决定辞掉工作去追求你的热情。

sentences.en: For example, deciding to quit your job to pursue your passion.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑有时会根据其自身的风险评估进行这种潜意识的计算，它会权衡回报或预期的收益与成本，与

sentences.en: Our brain will sometimes do this unconscious equation based on its own assessment of risk in which it will weigh up the rewards or the expected benefits versus the costs versus
sentences.zh: 本质上的风险进行对比。

sentences.en: kind of the risk essentially.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，因为有些人观察情况时，他们的大脑会自动变得规避风险。

sentences.en: And it's really interesting because there are people who will look at a situation and their brains will automatically be risk adverse.
sentences.zh: 本质上，这意味着他们不太可能去冒险。

sentences.en: Essentially, what this means means is that they are less likely to take a risk.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能关注潜在的后果或潜在的负面影响，而不是潜在的回报。

sentences.en: They are more likely to focus on the potential consequences or the potential downsides versus the potential reward.
sentences.zh: 也有一些人是风险偏好型的。

sentences.en: There are also people who are risk positive.
sentences.zh: 这就是你认识的那个朋友，他总是搬到新城市，总是准备好随时辞职，总是准备好搬家、环游

sentences.en: This is the friend that you know who is always moving to a new city, is always prepared to quit their job at the click of a finger, always prepared to move homes, to travel the
sentences.zh: 世界，去做一些我认为通常我们很多人会感到害怕、会犹豫不决的事情。

sentences.en: world, to do something that I think normally a lot of us would feel scared to do and would be I think hesitant to undertake.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有风险中性的人，他们会相当客观地看待事物。

sentences.en: And then of course there are people who are risk neutral who would see things I would say quite objectively.
sentences.zh: 他们相当均衡地权衡风险与回报。

sentences.zh: 这些风险的潜在损失是没有上限的。

sentences.en: So compared to bounded risks in which really you get to control how much you lose, unbounded risks, there is no limit.
sentences.zh: 所以与有界风险相比，在有界风险中你可以控制损失多少，而无界风险则是没有上限的。

sentences.en: So no matter what the potential payoff, which is not unlimited, it means that you're probably going to lose out on something pretty valuable.
sentences.zh: 因此，无论潜在回报如何（回报并非无限），这意味着你很可能会失去一些非常宝贵的东西。

sentences.en: I'd like to use this idea of jumping out of a plane having never skydived before.
sentences.zh: 我想用那个从未跳过伞就从飞机上跳下的例子来说明。

sentences.en: There is no limit to how much you could potentially lose in this situation, the limit being that you die, the limit being your life.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，你可能失去的程度是没有上限的，上限就是死亡，上限就是你的生命。

sentences.en: And the payoff is not that great.
sentences.zh: 而且回报并不那么诱人。

sentences.en: So when we think about it from that idea of utilitarianism that we were talking about before or from a cost-benefit analysis,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们从之前谈到的功利主义思想，或者从成本效益分析的角度来思考时，

sentences.en: the costs greatly outweigh the benefits.
sentences.zh: 成本远远超过了收益。

sentences.en: So it's important to be rational when we think about our approach to taking risks in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 因此，在思考20多岁时如何对待风险时，保持理性很重要。

sentences.en: Of course, I think this podcast and what I've been talking about is very risk-positive.

sentences.en: I truly do believe that the most amazing growth will come out of the periods of greatest discomfort where we really push ourselves and we really explore what's out there, but it
sentences.zh: 我真心相信，最惊人的成长将来自于最不适的时期，那时我们真正推动自己，真正探索外面的世界，但这

sentences.en: doesn't necessarily mean that you have to be silly about it or that you have to completely abandon all logic.

sentences.en: Taking a risk still requires judgment.

sentences.en: And yes, there are people who are more likely to take risks, but that doesn't necessarily mean that you should.
